BIE's content types (the type of an item decides its required questions and how it is taught, shown, played and drawn):
- process · Process: Something that happens in steps or stages over time: a mechanism, a procedure, a cycle (photosynthesis, cell division, how a bill becomes law). Required questions: how (kaise), when (kab). Other questions: what (kya), where (kahan), why (kyun), consequence (nateeja).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the result first (what it makes). 2) inputs and the place. 3) each step with its cause and its condition. 4) what breaks when a step fails. 5) the whole run once more at speed. 6) recap as a flow.
- structure · Structure: Something made of parts arranged in space, each part with a function (a cell, a leaf, the heart, a machine, the Parliament). Required questions: what (kya), where (kahan). Other questions: how (kaise), why (kyun), which (kaun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the whole in context. 2) zoom into each part in a fixed path (outside to inside). 3) function of each part tied to its shape. 4) how the parts work together. 5) labelled recap.
- classification · Classification: A group divided into kinds by a stated basis (types of tissues, kinds of rocks, kinds of writs). Required questions: which (kaun), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot), where (kahan).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the basis of division first. 2) the tree from the top down. 3) each kind with its identifying feature and an example. 4) the borderline cases and exceptions. 5) the tree as recap.
- comparison · Comparison: Two or more things set side by side on stated criteria (plant and animal cells, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha). Required questions: compare (tulna), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), why (kyun), evidence (saboot).
  Teaching pattern: 1) what is common. 2) criteria one at a time, both sides together. 3) the reason behind each difference. 4) the most confused pair named directly. 5) difference table as recap.
- timeline · Timeline: Events placed in time: history, the development of an idea, stages of a life (the Revolt of 1857, evolution of cell theory). Required questions: when (kab), why (kyun). Other questions: who (kaun), where (kahan), consequence (nateeja).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the period and its atmosphere. 2) events in order with their causes. 3) the people and their choices. 4) the turning point. 5) what changed after. 6) timeline recap.
- cause_effect · Reasoning (cause and effect): Why something happens: causes, effects, conditions and chains of reasoning (why tissues specialise, why prices rise, why a law was needed). Required questions: why (kyun), how (kaise). Other questions: consequence (nateeja), evidence (saboot), exception (tulna).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the effect students can see. 2) the cause. 3) each link of the chain with its mechanism. 4) the evidence. 5) the exception or limit. 6) the chain as recap.
- facts_numbers · Facts and numbers: Stated facts, quantities, measurements, statistics and formulas (heart rate 72 per minute, 3,000 against 50,000 soldiers at Plassey, F = ma). Required questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot). Other questions: compare (tulna), why (kyun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the fact in one line. 2) the number shown to scale against something familiar. 3) where it comes from (book or outside, dated). 4) what it changes or proves. 5) a formula built term by term when there is one.
- figure · Figure: A diagram, photo, map, graph or table drawing on the page whose content is visual (tissue pages 2, 7 and 8 are figures only). Required questions: what (kya), which (kaun). Other questions: how (kaise), why (kyun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) what the figure is and why it is here. 2) a reading path across it (labels in order). 3) the one thing to remember from it. 4) link back to the text it explains.
- definition · Definition: A term and its meaning as the book states it (tissue, meristem, sovereignty). Required questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot). Other questions: about (kya), why (kyun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) a concrete example first. 2) the book's definition word by word. 3) a non-example that tests the boundary. 4) where the term is used next in the chapter.

Prerequisites to teach (name · needed for · basis · why):
- Cell boundary, cytoplasm, nucleus and the cell as a functional unit · needed for c01, c02, c03, c06, c07, c08, c09, c10, c11, c12, c13, c14, c15, c16, c17, c18, c19, c20, c21, c22, c24, c25, c26, c27, c28, c29, c30, c31, c32, c33 · outside · Outside basis: Establish what belongs inside one cell, what lies outside it, and why a cell can have a specialised function; revisit nucleus position and number before interpreting epithelial, muscle, blood and plant-cell drawings.
- Plant cell wall, plasma membrane, vacuole, chloroplast and chlorophyll · needed for c04, c05, c22, c24, c25, c26, c27, c28, c30, c31, c32, c33, c36, c38, c39, c41, c42 · outside · Outside basis: Teach the wall–membrane distinction, a vacuole as an internal compartment, and chloroplasts containing chlorophyll so wall strength, vacuolation, photosynthesis and tissue viability can be understood.
- Part–whole relationships, classification trees and diagram conventions · needed for c02, c05, c06, c11, c13, c15, c16, c17, c18, c20, c21, c23, c25, c26, c27, c28, c32 · outside · Outside basis: Practise parent groups and subgroups, labels and leader lines, identification arrows versus transport arrows, and lengthwise versus cross-sectional views before reading the chapter's charts and tissue panels.
- Chromosomes, homologous pairs, chromatids, centromeres and ploidy · needed for c03, c04 · outside · Outside basis: Use a homologous pair to distinguish diploid from haploid sets and chromosome number from DNA quantity; this is essential for understanding daughter-cell outcomes and detecting the inaccurate doubling row.
- DNA replication, division phases, spindle, centrioles, asters and cytokinesis · needed for c03, c04, c22 · outside · Outside basis: Explain DNA replication before division, chromosome separation through prophase/metaphase/anaphase/telophase, and separation of cytoplasm; introduce microtubules, spindle poles, centrioles and asters before comparing plant and animal division.
- Somatic cells, germ line, gametes, spores and the plant life cycle · needed for c03, c04 · outside · Outside basis: Distinguish growth and tissue renewal from reproductive lineages, and explain why the book's meiosis-produces-gametes statement needs qualification for plants.
- Body surfaces, cavities, hollow-organ lumen, ducts and basal versus exposed surfaces · needed for c06, c07, c08, c09, c10, c11 · outside · Outside basis: Locate a lining relative to the lumen and the underlying tissue, and distinguish a secreting gland from its duct; this gives meaning to epithelial shape and layer comparisons.
- Locations of the digestive, respiratory, urinary and reproductive structures named in the tables · needed for c06, c08, c09, c10, c16, c18, c19 · outside · Outside basis: Briefly locate air sacs, capillaries, Bowman's capsule, proximal convoluted tubules, bladder, ureters, urethra, mouth, vagina, mammary/sweat/salivary glands, uterus, larynx, trachea and vocal cords so tissue-location facts have an anatomical setting.
- Diffusion, absorption, secretion, mucus, cilia and microvilli · needed for c07, c08, c09, c10, c11, c42 · outside · Outside basis: Distinguish movement down a concentration gradient, uptake and release; explain that cilia move surface material whereas microvilli increase surface area, allowing students to connect epithelial features to functions.
- Epithelial regeneration, keratin, abrasion and tight junctions · needed for c09, c10, c11 · outside · Outside basis: Explain replacement of shed cells, frictional wear, a keratin-rich protective surface and close cell junctions before interpreting stratified, keratinised and transitional epithelia.
- Extracellular matrix, proteins, polysaccharides and glycoproteins · needed for c12, c13, c14, c19, c20 · outside · Outside basis: Explain that extracellular material lies outside cells and can contain a hydrated carbohydrate-rich background and protein fibres; distinguish this matrix from cytoplasm and a muscle fibre.
- Tension, tensile strength, flexibility, elasticity, recoil and rigidity · needed for c12, c13, c15, c19, c20, c26, c27, c28, c43 · outside · Outside basis: Use pulling, bending and stretching examples to distinguish resistance to tension from recovery of shape, making connective fibres, cartilage, bone and plant supporting walls understandable.
- Skeleton, bones, joints, tendons, ligaments and muscle pull · needed for c06, c15, c18, c19, c43 · outside · Outside basis: Establish how muscles act across joints and how tendon and ligament attachments differ before interpreting movement, posture, dense connective tissue and the attachment question.
- Contraction, relaxation, cellular energy use, fatigue and voluntary control · needed for c14, c15, c16, c17, c18, c40 · outside · Outside basis: Define active force production, reduced active tension, fatigue as reduced performance and conscious control; use these definitions to compare muscle types without treating fatigue-resistance claims as unconditional.
- Heart pumping, blood pressure, blood vessels, pupil size and hair erection · needed for c16, c17, c18, c19, c40 · outside · Outside basis: Connect repeated heart-wall contraction to circulation and smooth-muscle contraction to hollow-organ propulsion, vessel calibre, iris action and the small hair-erector muscles.
- Blood plasma, red cells, white cells, platelets and lymph · needed for c06, c19, c20 · outside · Outside basis: Introduce blood's fluid matrix, oxygen transport, defence and clotting roles, and lymph as a tissue-fluid-related circulating fluid before locating these tissues in the animal classification and blood panel.
- Phagocytosis, antibodies, inflammation and connective-tissue cell identities · needed for c13, c20 · outside · Outside basis: Give brief meanings for engulfing particles, antibody-mediated defence and inflammatory responses so macrophage, neutrophil, monocyte, lymphocyte, plasma-cell, mast-cell and basophil labels have a concrete context; introduce fibroblasts as matrix-producing cells and mesenchymal cells as precursor cells.
- Bone cells, cartilage cells, matrix mineralisation and nutrient delivery · needed for c19, c20 · outside · Outside basis: Distinguish osteocytes from chondrocytes and rigid mineralised bone matrix from supportive cartilage matrix; explain why vessels and fine channels matter in the compact-bone illustration.
- Fat storage, lipid droplets, heat transfer and insulation · needed for c06, c13, c19, c20, c34 · outside · Outside basis: Connect a large intracellular lipid droplet to displaced adipocyte contents, stored energy, cushioning and reduced heat loss, supporting both the adipose drawings and the HPAS question.
- Stimulus, nerve impulse, cell-membrane electrical changes, synapse and neurotransmitter · needed for c06, c21 · outside · Outside basis: Define an incoming stimulus and explain that an impulse travels along the neuron's membrane while a chemical synapse uses a released messenger, so students can interpret the electrical-signal arrows and answer how another cell receives the message.
- Root, shoot, stem, leaf base, node, internode, bark, length and girth · needed for c05, c22, c23, c24, c35 · outside · Outside basis: Locate plant growth regions and distinguish elongation from increased thickness; this prevents confusion between apical, intercalary and lateral meristems.
- Cell differentiation, living protoplast, primary and secondary walls, cellulose and lignin · needed for c24, c25, c26, c27, c28, c29, c30, c31, c32, c33, c36, c38 · outside · Outside basis: Explain how specialised cells differ in contents and wall deposition, why lignified walls can function after cell death, and why a lumen is an internal cavity rather than a space between cells.
- Photosynthesis, food storage, chloroplast-bearing tissue and root mineral uptake · needed for c25, c26, c28, c29, c30, c31, c33, c39, c42 · outside · Outside basis: Establish that leaves can manufacture sugars, plant cells can store food, and roots take up water and minerals, giving a functional basis for chlorenchyma, parenchyma, xylem and phloem.
- Air spaces, density, displacement and buoyancy · needed for c25, c39 · outside · Outside basis: Explain how air-filled spaces reduce average density and help support aquatic plant parts in water, distinguishing aerenchyma from chlorophyll-containing parenchyma.
- Dicots, monocots, petiole, tendril, epidermis, hypodermis, cortex, pith, medullary rays, bundle sheath and pericycle · needed for c25, c26, c27, c28, c32, c36 · outside · Outside basis: Provide a simple position-based glossary for the many plant occurrence terms so the comparative table can be understood spatially rather than memorised as unexplained names.
- Vascular bundle, cambium, pits, perforations, sieve plates and plasmodesmata · needed for c30, c31, c32, c33, c37 · outside · Outside basis: Distinguish water-conducting wall openings, sieve-tube end partitions and cytoplasmic connections, and locate dividing cambium between the illustrated xylem and phloem.
- Transpiration, source–sink relations and wall versus membrane permeability · needed for c30, c31, c32, c33 · outside · Outside basis: Explain the setting for upward water transport, food movement from producing or releasing regions to using or storing regions, and the distinction between passage through conducting spaces and selective membrane transport.
- Plant cuticle, epidermal protection, cork and suberin · needed for c41 · outside · Outside basis: Supply the textbook explanation absent from the prose for the waxy-surface question and distinguish an outer tissue layer from a protective wall substance.
- Stomatal pore, guard cells, turgor and gas diffusion · needed for c42 · outside · Outside basis: Explain the difference between the opening used for gas exchange and the cells that regulate it, providing the missing conceptual basis for the leaf-gas-exchange question.
- Evaluating statement combinations, exclusions and restrictive words · needed for c34, c35, c36, c37, c38, c39, c40, c41, c42, c43 · outside · Outside basis: Practise checking each statement before choosing a combination, spotting words such as only, and answering except or incorrect stems; this avoids reversing what the examination question asks.

Exam focus:
- c01: Book basis: Tissue definition and division of labour anchor classification and function questions.
- c02: Book basis: The cell-to-organism hierarchy is suitable for ordering and part–whole questions.
- c03: Book basis: Division count, daughter-cell count, ploidy, crossing over and equational/reductional division are high-value comparisons. Outside clarification: The inaccurate DNA/chromosome row requires correction before exam use.
- c04: Book basis: Cell plate versus cleavage furrow, centrioles, asters and division sites support direct comparison and matching questions.
- c05: Book basis: The complete plant-tissue hierarchy supplies subgroup, example and odd-one-out questions.
- c06: Book basis: Four main animal tissues, their functions and the connective-tissue subgroups are core classification material.
- c07: Book basis: Tight packing, basement membrane, barrier function and gland formation distinguish epithelium from connective tissue.
- c08: Book basis: Shape–location–function matching for squamous, cuboidal and columnar epithelia is directly testable.
- c09: Book basis: Surface-cell shape, multiple layers, gland ducts and protective functions support identification questions.
- c10: Book basis: Pseudostratification, keratinisation and stretchable urothelium provide distinctive comparison facts.
- c11: Book basis: Figures test recognition by layers, shape, cilia and nuclear arrangement.
- c12: Book basis: Matrix consistency and collagen, elastic and reticulate fibres connect structure with support, strength and elasticity.
- c18: Book basis: Muscle location, function, striations, branching, nucleus number/position and control are major comparison targets, including the cardiac-muscle practice question.
- c19: Book basis: Connective-tissue locations, functions and examples support matching questions and the HPAS adipose-tissue question.
- c20: Book basis: Blood-cell names, Haversian canals, canaliculi, chondrocytes and adipocyte features are distinctive figure-based facts.
- c21: Book basis: Neuron parts, signal direction and synaptic junctions answer the chapter's explicit how-question. Outside clarification: Chemical transmission across a typical synapse completes the explanation.
- c23: Book basis: Apical, lateral and intercalary location–growth pairings are directly assessed, especially root tips only versus root and shoot tips.
- c24: Book basis: Differentiation and meristematic-versus-permanent contrasts are fundamental. Outside clarification: Generic wall and division claims require careful qualification.
- c25: Book basis: Parenchyma, chlorenchyma and aerenchyma provide storage, photosynthesis and buoyancy associations, including a direct practice question.
- c26: Book basis: Living cells, corner thickening, flexibility, leaf stalks and climber examples identify collenchyma.
- c27: Book basis: Lignified walls, dead cells, fibres/sclereids, seed coverings and coconut husk support direct identification and example questions.
- c28: Book basis: The eight-criterion simple-tissue comparison is a major source for statement, matching and odd-one-out questions.
- c30: Book basis: Xylem's four components and their separate conduction, storage and supporting roles are directly tested.
- c31: Book basis: Phloem components, food transport and the dead-fibre exception are high-value classification facts.
- c32: Book basis: Component identification, sieve plates, pits, cambium and transport-arrow interpretation support diagram questions.
- c33: Book basis: Xylem–phloem comparisons are central exam material. Outside clarification: Component-level exceptions prevent incorrect absolute statements about dead cells, wall chemistry and support.
- c34: Book basis: The explicitly attributed HPAS 2020 question tests heat conservation by subcutaneous adipose tissue.
- c36: Book basis: This practice question combines simple-tissue features. Outside clarification: Its ambiguous climber statement requires explanation rather than an unsupported universal rule.
- c41: Book basis: The practice question tests protective plant covering. Outside clarification: Epidermis and cuticle explain the intended answer despite the unclear thickest wording.
- c42: Book basis: The question explicitly tests the leaf gas-exchange site. Outside clarification: Distinguishing stomatal pores from guard cells resolves the main distractor.
- c43: Book basis: The chapter explicitly asks about muscle-to-bone attachment. Outside clarification: Tendon versus ligament is the essential attachment distinction.

videos.title: Cell से tissue और पूरे organism तक
videos.goal: पहले एक cell में boundary, cytoplasm और nucleus को समझेंगे: boundary के अंदर cell के अपने हिस्से हैं, जबकि बाहर दूसरी cells या material हो सकता है। फिर काम बाँटने वाले cells के example से tissue की book definition खोलेंगे और एक साथ मौजूद अलग tissues को एक ही tissue मानने की गलती जाँचेंगे। Cell → tissue → organ → organ system → organism को एक organ के अंदर और बाहर zoom करके जोड़ेंगे। Animal-tissue overview में classification का basis, 4 main groups, उनके काम और connective-tissue branches को figure के labels के क्रम में पढ़ेंगे। यह overview पहचान की शुरुआत करेगा; हर branch की पूरी पढ़ाई आगे होगी।

videos.title: Epithelial tissue: cell की shape, layers और काम
videos.goal: पहले body surface, lumen, basal side और exposed side को एक खोखली tube के example से समझेंगे। Diffusion, absorption और secretion को अलग examples से खोलेंगे। फिर epithelial sheet को exposed side से basement membrane और नीचे के tissue तक पढ़ेंगे: close packing, barrier और gland formation का काम बताएँगे। Simple epithelial types में हर book-listed shape, location और function को साथ जोड़ेंगे। Stratified types में layers के बाद exposed cells की shape से naming समझेंगे और book की सभी locations को body के छोटे location map पर रखेंगे। आखिर में simple और stratified का common काम, layer count, protection और exchange की तुलना करेंगे।

videos.title: Epithelial figures: दिखने वाली layers और असली layers
videos.goal: Pseudostratified, keratinised और transitional epithelia को पहले epithelial sheets के common frame में रखेंगे। फिर layer count, nucleus arrangement, surface features, stretch और book-listed locations पर एक-एक criterion से तुलना करेंगे। Pseudostratified का कई layers जैसा दिखना और वास्तव में cells का basal attachment अलग समझेंगे। Keratinisation, cilia और microvilli के काम अलग रखेंगे। c11 के हर figure में reading path exposed side → cell shape → nuclei → basal side रहेगा; पहचान के हर claim के लिए दिखाई देने वाला feature बताएँगे। Comparison table और labelled figure recap से समाप्त करेंगे।

videos.why_this_unit: c10 के सबसे आसानी से confuse होने वाले features को c11 की figures में तुरंत जाँचना सही visual identification सिखाता है। पिछली video के lumen, basal side, keratin, cilia और cell replacement को छोटे recall से फिर जोड़ेंगे।

videos.title: Connective tissue: cells के बाहर का material क्या करता है?
videos.goal: Epithelium की close packing से connective tissue की matrix वाली arrangement की तुलना शुरू करेंगे। बाहर से अंदर पढ़ते हुए matrix का background material, cells और collagen, elastic तथा reticulate fibres को book के अनुसार खोलेंगे। Protein, polysaccharide और glycoprotein के सरल outside meanings पहले देंगे। खींचने, मोड़ने और छोड़ने के examples से tensile strength, flexibility, elasticity और recoil अलग करेंगे। c13 की पूरी illustration में हर cell और fibre label का क्रम तय करेंगे; fibroblast से matrix, defence cells से उनके काम और adipocyte से lipid storage जोड़ेंगे। आखिर में cells और matrix के साथ काम करने का labelled recap होगा।

videos.title: Blood, bone, cartilage और fat: अलग matrix, अलग काम
videos.goal: Connective-tissue types का common आधार पहले रखेंगे। फिर c19 की हर row में location, cells, matrix और function पर दोनों या अधिक types को साथ पढ़ेंगे। Bone और cartilage से पहले osteocyte, chondrocyte, mineralisation और nutrient delivery समझेंगे। c20 के blood, compact bone, cartilage, areolar और adipose figures में हर label और पहचानने वाला feature पढ़ेंगे; canals, canaliculi और cell spaces को अलग करेंगे। HPAS 2020 question में skin के नीचे fat से कम heat loss का cause–effect chain बनाएँगे, विकल्पों की हर statement जाँचेंगे और insulation का मतलब heat बनाना नहीं होने की सीमा (limit) समझेंगे।

Evaluating statement combinations, exclusions and restrictive words
videos.opening_hook: Blood बहता है और bone सख्त है। दोनों connective tissue कैसे हो सकते हैं?
videos.story_or_analogy: गरम चीज़ के चारों ओर insulation रखने का example heat loss कम होने को समझाएगा। इसे Outside clarification कहकर subcutaneous adipose tissue से जोड़ेंगे।

videos.title: Muscle कैसे force बनाती है? Skeletal और smooth muscle

videos.title: Cardiac muscle, 3 muscle types और attachment questions
videos.goal: Heart की pumping से शुरू करके cardiac wall, branching fibres, striations, nuclei और book में दिखाए junctions को क्रम से पढ़ेंगे। फिर skeletal, cardiac और visceral muscles का common काम रखकर location, shape, branching, striations, nucleus number और position, control, function तथा fatigue पर criterion-wise तुलना करेंगे। Fatigue-resistance को unconditional claim नहीं बनाएँगे। c40 में incorrect statement खोजने से पहले हर statement का कारण जाँचेंगे। c43 में muscle pull से tendon का muscle-to-bone attachment और ligament का bone-to-bone attachment दोबारा दिखाएँगे; दोनों practice questions का recap feature और location से होगा।

videos.title: Neuron: message कहाँ से आता है और आगे कैसे जाता है?

videos.title: Mitosis और meiosis: chromosome गिनती सही कैसे रखें?
videos.goal: Chromosome, homologous pair, chromatid, centromere और ploidy को छोटे labelled model से पहले समझेंगे। फिर DNA replication, spindle और division phases का क्रम पढ़ेंगे; somatic cells, germ line, gametes, spores और plant life cycle का ज़रूरी फर्क बताएँगे। Mitosis और meiosis में common starting ideas के बाद division count, daughter-cell count, chromosome sets, crossing over और equational तथा reductional outcomes को साथ पढ़ेंगे। Replication और chromosome number को अलग गिनकर inaccurate printed row को Outside clarification से सुधारेंगे। Plant meiosis के बारे में gamete वाला absolute claim qualify करेंगे। फिर plant और animal division में centrioles, asters, sites और cell plate बनाम cleavage furrow की तुलना करेंगे।

videos.title: Differentiation से parenchyma, chlorenchyma और aerenchyma तक

videos.title: Collenchyma और sclerenchyma: मुड़ने वाला और सख्त support

videos.goal: Parenchyma, collenchyma और sclerenchyma का common simple-tissue basis पहले रखेंगे। फिर book की सभी 8 comparison criteria को एक-एक करके तीनों columns में साथ पढ़ेंगे। हर difference की वजह wall, cell contents, spaces, location या function से समझाएँगे। सबसे confuse होने वाले pairs—chlorenchyma तथा aerenchyma और collenchyma तथा sclerenchyma—सीधे पहचानेंगे। c36 में हर statement अलग जाँचेंगे; climber wording के intended tissue और उसके ambiguous absolute meaning में फर्क बताएँगे। Outside clarification को mark करेंगे और unsupported universal rule नहीं बनाएँगे। अंत में पूरी comparison table student से भरवाएँगे।
videos.opening_hook: अगर question में living cells, wall thickening और climber एक साथ लिखे हों, तो तुम हर statement कैसे जाँचोगे?
videos.why_this_unit: c28 की 8-criterion comparison को अपना समय देने से कोई row छूटती नहीं। c36 उसी table को statement evaluation में बदलता है और unclear wording को समझने की जगह देता है।

videos.title: Complex tissues: xylem और phloem की पूरी team
videos.goal: Simple और complex tissue का classification basis पहले रखेंगे: complex tissue में अलग cell types मिलकर shared work करते हैं। Water तथा minerals और food transport के context के बाद vascular bundle तथा openings के outside basics पढ़ेंगे। Xylem के 4 components में हर एक की shape, wall, living या dead condition और conduction, storage या support का काम खोलेंगे। Phloem की component tree में हर component और उसका काम पढ़ेंगे, खासकर living cells की generalisation में dead-fibre exception। Pits, perforations, sieve plates और plasmodesmata का फर्क छोटे labelled views से बताएँगे। Classification trees और component–function recap देंगे।
prerequisites_taught: Vascular bundle, cambium, pits, perforations, sieve plates and plasmodesmata
Transpiration, source–sink relations and wall versus membrane permeability
videos.opening_hook: Water और food ले जाने वाला tissue सिर्फ pipe होता है, या उसमें storage और support करने वाली cells भी होती हैं?
videos.story_or_analogy: अलग काम करने वाली transport team से complex tissue का shared function समझाएँगे। फिर हर actual component को उसके अलग काम से जोड़ेंगे।
videos.why_this_unit: c29 classification का basis देता है, फिर c30 और c31 दोनों branches को component level पर पूरा पढ़ाते हैं। Transport arrows पढ़ने से पहले source–sink और transpiration का अर्थ समझना ज़रूरी है।

videos.title: Xylem–phloem figures, transport arrows और comparison
videos.goal: c32 के हर panel में पहले बताएँगे कि figure क्या दिखाती है और क्यों है। Whole vascular bundle से cambium, xylem, phloem और component close-ups तक fixed reading path रखेंगे; हर supplied label पढ़ेंगे। Identification arrows और transport arrows अलग करेंगे। Longitudinal तथा cross-sectional views को जोड़ेंगे। फिर xylem और phloem का common transport role रखकर material, direction, components, living condition, walls और support पर book की तुलना पढ़ेंगे। Printed table की absolute generalisations को component exceptions से qualify करेंगे। c37 में हर option को component tree में रखकर excluded component चुनने का तरीका पढ़ेंगे।
videos.opening_hook: Figure में arrow ऊपर जाए तो क्या वह हमेशा water flow ही दिखा रहा है? पहले कैसे जाँचोगे?
videos.why_this_unit: c32 पहले सीखे components को visual arrangement देता है। c33 उसी evidence से comparison करता है और c37 classification की boundary जाँचता है।

videos.title: Plant की outer covering: epidermis, cuticle और protection
videos.goal: c41 के question से outer protection का context रखेंगे। पहले Outside clarification में epidermis, plant cuticle, cork और suberin को एक-दूसरे से अलग करके पढ़ेंगे। Outside से अंदर के क्रम में waxy cuticle → epidermal cells → नीचे के tissue का simple view बनाएँगे और हर हिस्से का काम बताएँगे। Protective tissue और protective substance का फर्क example तथा non-example से जाँचेंगे। फिर question के हर option को सही category और location में रखेंगे। Thickest wording के unclear होने को साफ बताएँगे; intended protective-covering concept समझाएँगे और उससे कोई universal thickness rule नहीं बनाएँगे।
prerequisites_taught: Plant cuticle, epidermal protection, cork and suberin
videos.opening_hook: Leaf के बाहर waxy protection है। क्या उस waxy material और उसे बनाने वाली cell layer का नाम एक ही है?
videos.why_this_unit: c41 के लिए chapter prose से बाहर का ज़रूरी base अलग से पढ़ाना पड़ता है। यह video protective layer, material और question की unclear wording को पर्याप्त जगह देता है।

videos.title: Stomata: gas कहाँ से जाती है और opening कौन बदलता है?
videos.goal: Leaf की epidermis में stomatal apparatus को whole context में रखेंगे। बाहर से pore, उसके दोनों ओर guard cells और अंदर के air spaces तक reading path देंगे। Outside clarification में turgor का सरल अर्थ और pore opening से उसका link समझाएँगे; gas movement के लिए diffusion को फिर example से जोड़ेंगे। Light या photosynthesis का मतलब stomata हमेशा खुले होने का universal rule नहीं बनाएँगे। c42 में gas-exchange site और उसे regulate करने वाली cells का फर्क हर option पर लागू करेंगे। आखिरी labelled recap में epidermis, cuticle, pore और guard cells के अलग काम पढ़ेंगे और chapter के structure–location–function frame से जोड़ेंगे।
prerequisites_taught: Stomatal pore, guard cells, turgor and gas diffusion
videos.opening_hook: Gas guard cells से होकर जाती है या उनके बीच की opening से? दोनों के काम कैसे अलग हैं?
videos.story_or_analogy: Door opening और उसे खोलने-बंद करने वाले हिस्से का फर्क pore तथा guard cells के अलग roles समझाएगा। Actual movement को turgor से अलग समझाएँगे।
videos.why_this_unit: c42 को c41 के बाद रखने से epidermis के अंदर pore की जगह साफ रहती है। अलग video से missing prerequisite पढ़ता है और pore–guard-cell confusion पूरी तरह जाँची जाती है।

output.chapter_flow: v1 cell, tissue और part–whole hierarchy से animal tissues का map बनाता है। v2–v3 epithelial tissues को shape, layers, locations और figures से खोलते हैं। v4–v5 connective tissue में matrix से types, visual पहचान और heat-loss question तक जाते हैं। v6–v7 muscle contraction से 3 muscle types, cardiac comparison और attachment questions तक पहुँचते हैं। v8 neuron की labelled बनावट (structure) और पूरे message route को जोड़ता है। v9 division के prerequisites पढ़ाकर mitosis, meiosis और plant–animal cytokinesis समझाता है। इसके बाद v10 plant classification और meristems, v11 differentiation तथा parenchyma, v12 support tissues और v13 सभी simple tissues की पूरी comparison पढ़ाते हैं। v14 complex tissues के components समझाता है और v15 उनके figures, transport तथा table की limits जाँचता है। v16–v17 protective covering और stomatal gas exchange के लिए ज़रूरी outside basics पढ़ाकर बाकी practice questions पूरे करते हैं। हर video में पहले prerequisite का simple example, फिर concept के content-type pattern में explanation, फिर figure या comparison recap और जहाँ जुड़ा है वहाँ practice question आएगा। Detailed scripts में हर beat के साथ उसका concept ID और सच में answer किया गया teacher question दर्ज होगा। Conditions और setting जहाँ काम समझाती हैं, वहाँ पढ़ाई जाएँगी; structure या classification पर बिना वजह process का क्रम नहीं थोपा जाएगा।
